No. kg never calls an LLM itself and needs no API keys (decision:no-embedded-llm, 'No LLM inside kg', RF-24, justifies package:kg). External agents (e.g. Claude Code, Codex) read the documents and decisions themselves, following the guide that ships with the package (package:kg.agents: `kg guide`, exported as the kg-graph skill with `kg guide --skill`). They write what they find as JSON valid against the schema and send it to kg, which validates it and merges it into the .kg store with `kg add` (kg.merge.add_to_store). Their nodes carry provenance method 'llm', and on merge a parser provenance wins over an llm or manual one (decision:parser-wins-over-llm), so this enrichment cannot wipe deterministic data.
